# Issue #7: touching intervals are not merged

`merge_intervals([(1, 3), (3, 5)])` returns `[(1, 3), (3, 5)]` but the documented
behaviour is that closed intervals sharing an endpoint merge into `[(1, 5)]`.
Unsorted input must also be handled. Fix `ranges/merge.py`.


Repository files:
ranges/__init__.py
ranges/merge.py
tests/test_merge.py

   2|     """Merge a list of closed integer intervals (start, end).
   3|     Touching intervals, e.g. (1,3) and (3,5), merge into (1,5).
   4|     Input may be unsorted. Returns a sorted list of tuples."""
   5|     if not intervals:
   6|         return []

arguments.summary: Fixed `ranges/merge.py` with two changes: (1) the merge condition was `start < last_end`, which failed to merge touching closed intervals like (1,3) and (3,5); changed it to `start <= last_end` so shared endpoints merge. (2) The function assumed sorted input; it now sorts the intervals (as tuples) before merging, so unsorted input is handled correctly. Verified with the existing test suite (both tests pass) and manual edge cases: touching, unsorted, nested, empty, and disjoint inputs all produce the expected results.
